A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SVRaster and contain complete, readable main texts and appendices. Text extraction and visual inspection support comparison of their methods, equations, tables, figures and proofs.

before.justification: v1 reports original novel-view synthesis, mesh reconstruction and ablation results in Section 4 and Appendices D–E.

after.justification: v2 retains original experimental results and reports revised synthesis results, additional efficiency measurements and feature-fusion demonstrations.

M1.justification: The voxel representation, rasterization procedure, objectives, adaptive pruning/subdivision and TSDF/Marching Cubes pipeline remain unchanged. The Morton-order terminology changes, while the new feature/semantic fusion illustrations do not specify a revised algorithm.

E1.justification: Figure 1 adds qualitative demonstrations of lifting RADIO features and Segformer semantics into 3D voxel fields. The existing synthesis and mesh datasets remain unchanged. Synthetic-NeRF results were already present in v1; their separate table in v2 does not represent new dataset coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain their baseline membership, including 3DGS, StopThePop, 3DGRT and EVER in Table 2, and the existing mesh-reconstruction comparators. RADIO and Segformer supply features for demonstrations. Changes to SVRaster's own configurations concern experimental variants.

E3.justification: The reported default supersampling changes from 1.1 to 1.5 and density learning rate from 0.05 to 0.025. v2 revises the fast-rendering configuration, replaces the large variant with a fast-training variant using a 0.3-scaled iteration schedule, and adds memory, model-size and 1x–3x resolution evaluation. Together these substantially expand and revise the experimental configurations.

E4.justification: v2 adds rendering-resolution sensitivity and resource-cost comparisons against 3DGS in Table 4, plus shortened-training quality/cost results. The adaptive-versus-uniform voxel study, existing hyperparameter and loss ablations, exposure failure case and mesh analyses remain, largely with renumbering.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run or seed counts, error bars, confidence intervals or significance tests. Reporting point estimates and averages across scenes remains the practice.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3 and the appendix's per-scene synthesis results are extensively revised. Table 1's base results change from 137 FPS, 12 minutes, 0.197 LPIPS and 27.10 dB PSNR to 121 FPS, 15 minutes, 0.185 and 27.33 dB under revised settings. Variant, resource and feature-fusion results are added; mesh scores and existing ablation values remain unchanged.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(25), representation definitions, derivatives and the Appendix B.3 induction proof retain the same mathematical content. Morton-order terminology, pseudocode naming and placement change without altering the reasoning.

C1.justification: Both versions claim fast neural-free adaptive voxel rendering, correct ordering without popping artifacts, over 4 dB PSNR and 10x FPS gains over previous voxel models, and compatibility with grid-based processing. The revised abstract reorders contributions and foregrounds existing capacity and broader application examples; the central claims remain.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 adds explanations of scene-dependent speed involving sorting width, covariance computation, ray–voxel intersections and contributing primitives per pixel. It explicitly discusses larger memory/model costs and interprets resolution scaling and revised quality rankings. Existing exposure-variation and surface-artifact limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 provides a code repository link and announces its release. Appendix C newly documents multiplying learning rates by 0.1 at iteration 19K, while Section 4.2 specifies the fast variants' settings and budget scaling. Most existing implementation details and the stated GPU remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds AM-RADIO and Segformer citations for the feature/semantic fusion illustrations. Earlier references and the substantive positioning against NeRF, Plenoxels, 3DGS and mesh-reconstruction methods are retained.

P1.justification: The abstract and Section 4.2 are locally rewritten, and 'dynamic Morton order' becomes 'direction-dependent Morton order' throughout. Acknowledgements move and an Updates block is added. The overall section and appendix organization remains substantially intact.

P2.justification: Figure 1's application panel is redesigned, Table 4 is added, and v1's Appendix Table 19 is split into Tables 20–21. Table 2 drops its rasterization-indicator row; Figure 8 and Listing 3 move. Other core figures and appendix qualitative images are retained.

improvement.justification: The added resource/resolution comparisons, fast-training results, explanatory discussion and code pointer make the method easier to assess and use. These gains are qualified by a new unexplained reporting mismatch: v2 Table 3 gives 366 FPS for DeepBlending, while Table 20 gives 297 and 308 FPS for its two scenes. This weakens confidence in part of the revised speed evidence.
